explanation: Wu rose from palace concubine to empress, then took the throne herself, proclaiming a new Zhou dynasty. Cixi dominated the late Qing court but ruled as regent, never as emperor.

claims.text: Wu Zetian was the only woman to rule China as emperor in her own right, proclaiming her own Zhou dynasty in 690.
Cixi and Empress Lü held power as empresses dowager or regents, and Yang Guifei was a consort of the 700s; none took the title of emperor.
Wu Zetian began as a concubine at the Tang court and became empress before taking the throne.
Empress Dowager Cixi dominated the late Qing court as regent but never ruled as emperor.

evidence.restatement: Wu began as a concubine at the Tang court, became Gaozong's empress, then took the throne.
Cixi controlled the late Qing court as regent, never as emperor.
Wu Zetian proclaimed her own Zhou dynasty in AD 690 and is the only woman to rule China as emperor in her own right.

claimResults.note: Rival test: Empress Lü and Cixi ruled as dowager or regent, Yang Guifei was a consort. A failed 653 rebel, Chen Shuozhen, styled herself emperor but never ruled China, so the 'only' holds.
